title: Descent of a finite module presentation along a given finite-type ring diagram
statement:
Let $I$ be a nonempty directed preordered set, $B:I	o\mathrm{CommRing}$ a ring diagram, and $\kappa_i:B_i	o S$ a colimit cocone [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Assume every $B_i$ is a finite-type $\mathbf Z$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $M$ be a finitely presented $S$-module (the cokernel of a map between finite free $S$-modules). Then there are a nonempty directed preordered set $J$, a final functor $F:J	o I$ (restriction along $F$ preserves colimits), an additive-group diagram $D:J	o\mathrm{Ab}$, compatible maps $
u_j:D_j	o M$, and $B_{Fj}$-module structures on $D_j$, such that: $M$ with these maps is a colimit of $D$; every $D_j$ is finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; for $i\le j$, the transition $d_{ji}$ obeys $d_{ji}(yx)=B(F(i	o j))(y)d_{ji}(x)$; $
u_j(yx)=\kappa_{Fj}(y)
u_j(x)$; the canonical maps $B_{Fj}\otimes_{B_{Fi}}D_i	o D_j$, $y\otimes x\mapsto yd_{ji}(x)$, and $S\otimes_{B_{Fj}}D_j	o M$, $y\otimes x\mapsto y
u_j(x)$, are module isomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. If the rings and indices live in universe $u$ and $M$ in universe $v$, the index set $J$ lives in $u$ and the groups $D_j$ can be chosen in $v$.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 00QX (lemma-limit-module-essentially-finite-presentation), presentation-matrix paragraph, non-local construction used in Tag 00R1

proof.text: Choose an explicit finite free presentation using Module.FinitePresentation.exists_fin'. Apply the concrete ring-colimit representative theorem to each standard-basis matrix entry. Finset induction and directedness give a common upper bound. Map all representatives to that stage, using cocone naturality. For an empty matrix the initial arbitrary index supplies the bound.
Apply the lifted-matrix construction theorem to obtain the final directed restriction, the small quotient diagram, its finite generators and both tensor base-change clauses.
Restrict the ring colimit cocone along F by Functor.Final.isColimitWhiskerEquiv. Apply the tensor-diagram elementwise theorem to get representatives of M and eventual zero in the stage modules.

Prove eventual equality of two representatives by moving to a common stage, subtracting and applying eventual zero. For any additive cocone, choose a representative of each element and take its cocone value. Eventual equality proves independence from representatives. Use common upper stages to prove additivity; zero comes from any zero representative. Bundle the resulting additive map as the universal cocone morphism. Independence proves factorization; representations prove uniqueness. The private additive_diagram_isColimit theorem implements this directly in arbitrary universes.

theorem exists_finitePresentation_module_diagram
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (B : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (S : Type u) [CommRing S]
    (κ : B ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj (CommRingCat.of S))
    (hκ : Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk (CommRingCat.of S) κ)))
    (hfinite : ∀ i, Algebra.FiniteType ℤ (B.obj i))
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M] [Module.FinitePresentation S M] :
    ∃ (J : Type u) (_ : Preorder J) (_ : Nonempty J) (_ : IsDirected J (· ≤ ·))
      (F : J ⥤ I) (_ : F.Final)
      (D : J ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{v})
      (ν : D ⟶ (Functor.const J).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of M))
      (_ : ∀ j, Module (B.obj (F.obj j)) (D.obj j)),
      Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk (AddCommGrpCat.of M) ν)) ∧
      (∀ (i j : J) (h : i ≤ j) (y : B.obj (F.obj i)) (x : D.obj i),
        (D.map (homOfLE h)).hom (y • x) =
          (B.map (F.map (homOfLE h))).hom y • (D.map (homOfLE h)).hom x) ∧
      (∀ j (y : B.obj (F.obj j)) (x : D.obj j),
        (@AddCommGrpCat.Hom.hom _ (AddCommGrpCat.of M) (ν.app j)) (y • x) =
          (@CommRingCat.Hom.hom _ (CommRingCat.of S) (κ.app (F.obj j))) y •
            (@AddCommGrpCat.Hom.hom _ (AddCommGrpCat.of M) (ν.app j)) x) ∧
      (∀ j, Module.Finite (B.obj (F.obj j)) (D.obj j)) ∧
      (∀ (i j : J) (h : i ≤ j),
        letI := (B.map (F.map (homOfLE h))).hom.toAlgebra
        ∃ e : B.obj (F.obj j) ⊗[B.obj (F.obj i)] D.obj i ≃ₗ[B.obj (F.obj j)] D.obj j,
          ∀ (y : B.obj (F.obj j)) (x : D.obj i),
            e (y ⊗ₜ[B.obj (F.obj i)] x) = y • (D.map (homOfLE h)).hom x) ∧
      (∀ j,
        letI := (@CommRingCat.Hom.hom _ (CommRingCat.of S) (κ.app (F.obj j))).toAlgebra
        ∃ e : S ⊗[B.obj (F.obj j)] D.obj j ≃ₗ[S] M,
          ∀ (y : S) (x : D.obj j),
            e (y ⊗ₜ[B.obj (F.obj j)] x) =
              y • (@AddCommGrpCat.Hom.hom _ (AddCommGrpCat.of M) (ν.app j)) x)
